# requires: store
#
# The machine stays awake for exactly as long as a lease is held on running
# work, and no longer. `hold` takes the platform's idle-sleep inhibitor for the
# lease the record carries, the way a runner does at claim. Every way a lease
# stops being one ends the hold: the holder letting go, the job turning
# terminal, the lease lapsing. A record whose lease is not live holds nothing,
# and a hold belongs to one epoch, so the same owner claiming again after a
# lapse does not revive it. The holder dying is the case a scenario cannot
# script and the one an inhibitor bound to a process gets for free.
#
# The hold learns of an ending through the watch layer, so an observation
# follows the ending by one poll.
submit A size=64 digest=good src=file
hold A
claim A alpha 5000
hold A
release A alpha
sleep 1000
state A
claim A alpha 5000
hold A
finish A alpha failed
sleep 1000
state A
submit B size=64 digest=good src=file
claim B alpha 1500
hold B
sleep 1900
state B
claim B alpha 1500
hold B
sleep 1900
claim B alpha 1500

# expect 2: awake=no
# expect 4: awake=yes
# expect 7: awake=no
# expect 9: awake=yes
# expect 12: awake=no
# expect 15: awake=yes
# expect 17: awake=no
# expect 19: awake=yes
# expect 21: ok state=running
# expect 21: awake=no
